Definition: a carcase (as limp), whether of man or beast; figuratively, an idolatrous image
BiblicalUsage: Peger is a carcase, a dead body left where it fell. David told Goliath that the carcases of the Philistines would feed the birds that day, and when Judah looked out over the enemy army they saw only dead bodies fallen to the earth, with none escaped.
TheologicalSignificance: What I hold is that God fights His own battles: the field of carcases is what is left when men trust in their own strength instead of in Him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
